level_1: Acquires and presents a basic pediatric physiatric history, including medical, functional, and psychosocial elements
level_2: Acquires and presents a comprehensive pediatric physiatric history identifying all components of functioning, including development, impairments, activities, participation, and contextual factors
level_3: Acquires and presents a relevant pediatric physiatric history in a prioritized fashion, integrating components of functioning within the context of development
level_4: Elicits and presents key pediatric physiatric history, including subtleties, in a prioritized and efficient fashion across a spectrum of ages and impairments
level_5: Role models the effective gathering and presentation of subtle and salient pediatric physiatric history from patients across a spectrum of ages and impairments

subcompetencies.name: Physical Examination for Pediatric Rehabilitation Patients

level_1: Performs and presents a basic pediatric physiatric examination
level_2: Performs and presents a comprehensive, developmentally appropriate pediatric physiatric examination
level_3: Performs and presents a hypothesis-driven pediatric physiatric examination, with identification of subtle or atypical findings over a spectrum of ages and impairments
level_4: Efficiently performs and presents a hypothesis- driven pediatric physiatric examination, with identification of subtle or atypical findings over a spectrum of ages and impairments
level_5: Role models a hypothesis-driven pediatric physiatric examination that identifies subtle or atypical findings over a spectrum of ages and impairments

subcompetencies.name: Differential Diagnosis of Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Patients

level_1: Produces a basic differential diagnosis for common pediatric physiatric disorders and associated conditions
level_2: Generates a comprehensive differential diagnosis that includes pediatric physiatric disorders and associated conditions
level_3: Develops a focused, age- appropriate differential diagnosis, including pediatric medical conditions and less common conditions
level_4: Produces a prioritized differential diagnosis across a spectrum of ages and impairments
level_5: Efficiently produces a focused and prioritized differential diagnosis accounting for rare conditions

subcompetencies.name: Diagnostic Evaluation of Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Patients

level_1: Orders appropriate diagnostic studies for conditions commonly seen in pediatric physiatry (e.g., dysplastic hip), based on established guidelines or consensus
Orders diagnostic testing and assessment tools based on cost effectiveness and likelihood that results will influence clinical management (e.g., gait analysis)
level_2: Orders comprehensive, hypothesis-driven diagnostic studies for conditions commonly seen in pediatric physiatry
Integrates knowledge of functional goals, results of pediatric assessment tools, and prognosis to optimize patient management
level_3: Identifies common pediatric assessment tools and outcome measures
Streamlines testing for cost effectiveness and minimal patient and family burden
level_4: Appropriately prioritizes the sequence and urgency of diagnostic testing, and begins to interpret results to guide further management
Serves as a resource to others for the implementation of assessment tools and outcome measures
level_5: Uses appropriate outcome measures and scales for diagnoses

subcompetencies.name: Medical Management of Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Patients

level_1: Identifies and manages general medical conditions and their complications
level_2: Identifies and manages complications related to complex medical, neurological, and musculoskeletal disorders
level_3: Develops and implements a comprehensive evidence-based treatment plan that anticipates and addresses complications related to medical, neurological, and musculoskeletal disorders
level_4: Develops a treatment plan that anticipates and addresses complications across the spectrum of ages (e.g., complications that occur in adulthood from a childhood onset condition)
level_5: Role models the development and implementation of a comprehensive treatment plan, including consideration of emerging treatments

subcompetencies.name: Rehabilitation/Functional Management of Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Patients – Assistive Devices and

level_1: Evaluates patient need for common assistive devices and technologies based on impairment
level_2: Evaluates patient need for a full range of assistive devices and technologies based on impairments, accounting for barriers, contraindications, comorbidities, issues related to growth and development, and input from other professionals
level_3: Generates a detailed prescription, in consultation with other professionals, for a full range of assistive devices and technologies, including justification and advocacy where needed
level_4: Serves as a resource to other professionals for clinical problem solving and functional challenges related to assistive devices and technologies
level_5: Involved in research/development of novel assistive devices or technologies

subcompetencies.name: Rehabilitation/Functional Management of Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Patients – Rehabilitation

level_1: Prescribes common rehabilitation therapies for children based on impairments
level_2: Prescribes common rehabilitation therapies accounting for developmental needs and understanding expected goals
level_3: Generates specific therapy prescriptions, targeting for condition- specific goals and precautions
level_4: Monitors and adjusts the therapy interventions based on previous results and reassessment
level_5: Participates in research and development of novel therapy interventions

subcompetencies.name: Procedural Skills in Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine

level_1: Demonstrates basic understanding of indications for various spasticity procedures in pediatric patients
Modifies procedures to accommodate patient’s impairments and minimize discomfort; consistently performs procedures without attending direction
level_2: Performs procedures with hands-on assistance
Troubleshoots spasticity interventions that are ineffective or when complications arise
level_3: Provides basic education to patients and families regarding procedure- specific information and treatment options and obtains informed consent
Skillfully performs a wide variety of procedures and teaches others in the safe performance of these procedures
level_4: Performs procedures with verbal guidance
Effectively uses spasticity procedures in complex clinical scenarios
level_5: Selects spasticity procedures based on individual condition; provides in-depth education to patients and families regarding procedure-specific information and treatment options
Develops a curriculum

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of complex pediatric medical conditions and basic preventive care
level_2: Synthesizes physiatric knowledge of common pediatric rehabilitation disorders, secondary conditions, treatment options, and complications
level_3: Synthesizes physiatric knowledge of complex pediatric rehabilitation disorders, secondary conditions, treatment options, and complications
level_4: Integrates physiatric knowledge into practice across a spectrum of ages, impairments, educational and clinical scenarios
level_5: Serves as a resource for others for new and emerging concepts and investigation relevant to foundational principles of physiatric practice

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic growth and developmental milestones
Applies knowledge of developmental trajectory to provide a functional prognosis
level_2: Recognizes atypical growth or development (e.g., recognition of persistent primitive reflexes)
Synthesizes the knowledge of anatomy and physiology in the context of prevention and treatment (e.g., use of practice guidelines for osteopenia and hip dysplasia in cerebral palsy)
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of anatomy and physiology related to growth (e.g., bladder volume, skeletal immaturity, pubertal maturation)
Collaborates on the development of practice guidelines or educational resources for clinicians in the area of growth and development
level_4: Recognizes influence of development and impairment level on current functional capabilities
level_5: Applies knowledge of pathophysiology to the growth and development of a child (e.g., precocious puberty in brain disorders, hip dysplasia with cerebral palsy)

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
level_3: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_4: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
level_2: Describes quality improvement initiatives
level_3: Participates in quality improvement initiatives
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_5: Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates understanding and knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for the local population
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across different levels of health care and settings
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively collaborating with members of the interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide accessible and quality care for specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of the local population and community to minimize health care barriers
Leads quality improvement of transitions of care within and across different levels of health care and settings to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different professions and specialties
Leads innovations and advocacy in partnership with populations and communities experiencing health care barriers to make sustainable improvements

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the health care system, including the various venues for post-acute care
Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)
Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for independent practice
level_3: Identifies basic knowledge domains for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding, financial, personnel)
Engages with patients and families in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
level_4: Describes how components of a health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Identifies care plan that is compatible with each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type) and obstacles for delivery
Navigates the various components of the health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
Educates others to prepare them for transition to practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access available evidence
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Professional Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for professional development
Designs and implements a learning plan, with guidance
Uses data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan to address performance gaps and modifies accordingly
level_2: Identifies and/or acknowledges gaps between expectations and actual performance
Seeks and incorporates verbal feedback and other performance data intermittently, in an open and reflective manner
Role models consistent incorporation of verbal feedback and other performance data
level_3: Identifies opportunities to improve
Institutes behavioral changes to narrow performance gaps
Mentors others on reflective practice, including the design and implementation of learning plans
level_4: Demonstrates openness to verbal feedback and other performance data
Independently designs and implements a learning plan
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to performance gaps
Seeks and incorporates verbal feedback and other performance data consistently, with humility and adaptability

level_1: Approaches clinical care and educational duties with actions consistent with core ethical principles
level_2: Demonstrates consistent application of ethical principles in routine clinical practice, such as informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error reporting and disclosure, and stewardship of limited resources
level_3: Recognizes tensions between conflicting ethical principles in complex situations and seeks appropriate guidance to help resolve ethical dilemmas
level_4: Manages ethical dilemmas, using appropriate resources as needed to facilitate resolution (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_5: Serves as a resource for others to resolve complex ethical dilemmas

level_1: Describes when and how to appropriately report lapses
Takes remedial action to address lapses when applicable
level_2: Identifies professionalism lapses in oneself and others
Demonstrates professional behavior in all situations, including during times of stress
level_3: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations
Proactively intervenes to prevent lapses
level_4: Takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses when applicable and identifies contributing factors
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Anticipates situations that may trigger professionalism lapses
Addresses system issues to minimize potential for professionalism lapses

level_1: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete responsibilities
level_2: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_4: Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of persons, teams, and systems are met in a timely manner
level_5: Coaches others to optimize timely task completion

subcompetencies.name: Patient Care Etiquette with Patients of All Abilities

level_1: Recognizes the need to respect the dignity of all people regardless of impairments or disabilities
level_2: Demonstrates specific elements of verbal and physical communication that reflect respect for people with impairments or disabilities
level_3: Proactively maintains pediatric patient’s comfort and dignity during clinical encounters for those with mild impairments or disabilities
level_4: Proactively maintains pediatric patient’s comfort and dignity during clinical encounters for those with severe impairments or disabilities
level_5: Serves as a role model and resource by coaching others in behaviors and actions that optimize the comfort, dignity, and respect of people with impairments or disabilities

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being and demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors
level_3: With assistance, proposes, implements, and refines a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Independently develops, implements, and refines a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others and addresses system barriers and facilitators to optimize personal and professional well-being

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Organizes and initiates communication with the patient/patient’s family by clarifying expectations and verifying understanding of the clinical situation
Overcomes biases while proactively minimizing communication barriers
level_2: Minimizes common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability)
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters
Independently uses shared decision making to align patient/patient’s family values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Accurately communicates own role within the health care system
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Mentors others in developing positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information, elicits patient/patient’s family values, goals, and preferences, and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Role models self- awareness practice while teaching a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_5: Minimizes complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy), but has limited awareness of potential biases
Easily establishes therapeutic relationships, with attention to patient/patient’s family concerns and context, regardless of complexity
Practices skills including compassion and empathy for shared decision making in patient/patient’s family communication including those with a high degree of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Uses respectful language that values all members of the health care team
level_2: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
level_3: Identifies the need to adapt communication style, as needed, to fit team needs
level_4: Implements recommendations and communication from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
level_5: Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed

level_1: Demonstrates organized and complete clinical, diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Appropriately selects direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) forms of communication based on context
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of appropriate channels of communication within the institution (e.g., pager callback, timely response to emails)
Independently documents information in compliance with current regulatory health system requirements (e.g., Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, Joint Commission, institutional requirements)
level_3: Regularly updates the medical record, communicating clinical reasoning as care evolves (e.g., on-call evaluations, patient preferences, team/family meetings, conflict resolution, and advanced directives)
Produces written or verbal communication that serves as an example for others to follow
level_4: Communicates through appropriate channels as required by institutional policy (e.g., patient safety reports)
Serves as an expert resource in communication technology
level_5: Demonstrates effective and timely integration and dissemination of information among all available sources to facilitate patient-centered care, including anticipatory recommendations
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
